reads.what_it_sells: Repairboard is a digital board for a repair shop to track each repair’s stage and give customers a read-only link to view that status.
reads.relevance_feedback: The profile explicitly says I am considering how customers can inspect repair stages, and the email offers exactly that through a shared board and read-only customer links. The email additionally presupposes that a customer-visible board could suit my shop; whether it fits my existing workflow, repair volume, and customer communication process is unknown.
assumed_experiences: Profile-supported: I run an independent repair shop and am considering ways for customers to inspect repair stages.
Email-only: My shop could maintain repair stages on a shared digital board.
Email-only: Giving customers individual read-only status links would be useful in my workflow.
Unknown: What system or process I currently use to track repairs and update customers.
reads.problem_now: Customer access to repair-stage information is relevant to a decision I am currently considering, but the profile establishes no deadline, current communication failure, or urgency.
reads.biggest_doubt: I cannot tell whether using this would mean updating another separate board alongside whatever already tracks the repair, so the sample may show the presentation without answering the main effort question.
reads.to_click_it_would_have_to: I would have clicked if this email had told me whether the sample also shows how a shop updates a repair and whether that requires duplicate entry; the direct relevance and low-commitment sample are enough for me to click today anyway.
fixes: Rewrite “The sample shows this presentation directly: the shared board, the repair stages, and the customer-facing view.” as “The sample shows the shop board, how a repair moves between stages, and exactly what the customer sees.”
Cut “That gives you something concrete to assess before considering anything further.” because the preceding sentence already explains why I should view the sample.

Add after “A shop can share a read-only status link with its customer” a direct statement clarifying whether staff update Repairboard separately or whether it connects to an existing repair-tracking process.
